ratings.note: Mismatched names (Conductivity vs EC probe) are visible on every view but mainly trip novices and visitors (f2); the mapping takes a moment to work out (i1); once learned it stops mattering (p1). s=2.

Screenshot shows value plus verdict only, on all four reading cards, every check (f3); verdicts carry most of the task but 'Warm' leaves the needed action unclear (i1); the meaning of 'Warm' can be learned from the checklist, so it recurs but can be overcome (p1). s=3.

Chart in screenshot has time labels only, no pH axis or band (f2, used when checking for overnight drift); the cards' 'In range' verdict softens it, so it is mostly a misreading risk (i1); users learn to ignore the chart (p1). s=2.

Status cells are empty in the aria tree for all rows; only the screen-reader volunteer meets it (f0), but for them top task 3 is fully blocked on this page (i3), on every visit with no workaround (p2). s=4.

Colour-blind volunteers are on every rota and the table is checked several times per shift (f2); in the deuteranopia capture the red float fault is indistinguishable from green, so the faulty sensor is missed (i2); no text or shape to learn from (p2). s=4.

Forced-colours users are not named in the context and the bay iPad's Safari rarely uses forced colours (f0); for those users all status disappears (i3), every visit (p2). s=4; rated 3 because the user group in this setting is unevidenced and the colour-only failure is already captured separately.

Screenshot shows green 'Topped up 09:30' beside a red Reservoir float dot; arises whenever the float faults (f1); before reservoir work the user may trust the wrong signal (i2); a user can learn to check the table too, but the conflict is never explained (p1). s=3.

Forced-colours captures show only the label, no switch, in both states; few users in this context (f0); the critical control is hard to find, though the label and status sentence remain (i2); every visit (p2). s=3.

Probe shows one click restores automatic with no dialog; a stray tap on the shared wet-glove tablet during reservoir work is occasional (f1); the result is a dosing error the user may not notice (i2); same each time but users can be careful (p1). s=3.

Probe 4 after-reload screenshot shows the switch back on and 'automatic' text; the shared tablet is reloaded or checked by others during each reservoir change (f2); the critical safety setting is lost and pumps may dose an empty tank (i3); cannot be learned around (p2). s=4.

Two of five sensors are amber or red in the shipped data and hover reveals nothing (f2); novices cannot tell what is wrong or what to do and must find the lead (i2); experience reduces it but each new fault type recurs (p1). s=3.

Manual-state screenshot shows only the switch and history lines; met every manual session (f2); confusion about where pumps are started, likely answered by the controller or checklist (i1); learned after the first time (p1). s=2.
